<div class="honest">
<p>NVIDIA Warp is an excellent per-thread kernel compiler: it is the fastest arm in 2 of the 12 RK4 cells this card runs, and when every sample runs all 1000 steps it ties hawk + eagle: 1.71 ms against hawk + eagle's 1.74 ms.</p>
<p>On memory, hawk + eagle's lower-level building blocks go lighter than Warp: 1.2× the minimum against Warp's 1.8×. eagle.simulate keeps room to compact the batch and uses 1.1×.</p>
<p class="fine">Measured on NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3. <a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, every arm</a>.</p>

<div class="honest">
<p>NVIDIA Warp is an excellent per-thread kernel compiler: when every sample runs all 1000 steps hawk + eagle beats it: 103 ms against Warp's 119 ms.</p>
<p>On memory, hawk + eagle's lower-level building blocks go lighter than Warp: 1.1× the minimum against Warp's 1.8×. eagle.simulate keeps room to compact the batch and uses 1.1×.</p>
<p class="fine">Measured on NVIDIA L4. <a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, every arm</a>.</p>
</div>

<div class="honest">
<p>NVIDIA Warp is an excellent per-thread kernel compiler: it is the fastest arm in 1 of the 12 RK4 cells this card runs, and when every sample runs all 1000 steps hawk + eagle beats it: 4.83 ms against Warp's 6.67 ms.</p>
<p>On memory, hawk + eagle's lower-level building blocks go lighter than Warp: 1.1× the minimum against Warp's 1.8×. eagle.simulate keeps room to compact the batch and uses 1.1×.</p>
<p class="fine">Measured on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB. <a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, every arm</a>.</p>
</div>

<div class="honest">
<p>NVIDIA Warp is an excellent per-thread kernel compiler: when every sample runs all 1000 steps hawk + eagle beats it: 640 ms against Warp's 699 ms.</p>
<p>On memory, hawk + eagle's lower-level building blocks go lighter than Warp: 1.1× the minimum against Warp's 1.8×. eagle.simulate keeps room to compact the batch and uses 1.1×.</p>
<p class="fine">Measured on Quadro P2000. <a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, every arm</a>.</p>
</div>

<div class="honest">
<p>NVIDIA Warp is an excellent per-thread kernel compiler: when every sample runs all 1000 steps hawk + eagle beats it: 27.6 ms against Warp's 32.1 ms.</p>
<p>On memory, hawk + eagle's lower-level building blocks go lighter than Warp: 1.2× the minimum against Warp's 1.8×. eagle.simulate keeps room to compact the batch and uses 1.1×.</p>
<p class="fine">Measured on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. <a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, every arm</a>.</p>
</div>

<p class="axis-note radar-note">Outer is better on every axis; italic axes are qualitative scores (author's judgement); hover or tap an axis for its meaning.</p>
<p class="axis-note radar-note radar-caption-control">NVIDIA Warp gives you near-total control of every kernel, short of raw CUDA. raptor takes that control over on purpose, and that is where its speed on uneven batches comes from.</p>
<details class="radar-data radar-howto"><summary>How to read this radar</summary><p class="axis-note radar-note">Each measured axis is stretched over its own best-to-worst range, so ring labels differ per axis (compile time: fixed, 0.1 s to 100 s; code size: at least 4x). Axes are ordered so each tool's strengths sit together, so read the axes, not the area.</p><p class="axis-note radar-note">Qualitative axes are not measurements: hollow markers, a linear scale, and no marker where a tool has no reading. A hollow marker on compile time is the tool's simple-kernel time. The hover panel has each axis's full wording.</p><ul class="radar-howto-list"><li><strong>Tensor workloads</strong>: 5 = dense array maths, batched linear algebra and convolutions are its home ground.</li><li><strong>Array-style programming</strong>: 5 = the whole-array expression is the programming model.</li><li><strong>Half precision and below</strong>: 5 = FP16, BF16, FP8, FP4 and tensor cores are first-class paths.</li><li><strong>Low-level control</strong>: 5 = you write what each thread does and how it is launched.</li><li><strong>Single-thread abstraction</strong>: 5 = you write one sample and nothing else.</li></ul><p class="axis-note radar-note"><a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, in the full tables</a>.</p></details>

<p class="axis-note radar-note">Outer is better on every axis; italic axes are qualitative scores (author's judgement); hover or tap an axis for its meaning.</p>
<p class="axis-note radar-note radar-caption-control">NVIDIA Warp gives you near-total control of every kernel, short of raw CUDA. raptor takes that control over on purpose, and that is where its speed on uneven batches comes from.</p>
<details class="radar-data radar-howto"><summary>How to read this radar</summary><p class="axis-note radar-note">Each measured axis is stretched over its own best-to-worst range, so ring labels differ per axis (compile time: fixed, 0.1 s to 100 s; code size: at least 4x). Axes are ordered so each tool's strengths sit together, so read the axes, not the area.</p><p class="axis-note radar-note">Qualitative axes are not measurements: hollow markers, a linear scale, and no marker where a tool has no reading. A hollow marker on compile time is the tool's simple-kernel time. The hover panel has each axis's full wording.</p><ul class="radar-howto-list"><li><strong>Tensor workloads</strong>: 5 = dense array maths, batched linear algebra and convolutions are its home ground.</li><li><strong>Array-style programming</strong>: 5 = the whole-array expression is the programming model.</li><li><strong>Half precision and below</strong>: 5 = FP16, BF16, FP8, FP4 and tensor cores are first-class paths.</li><li><strong>Low-level control</strong>: 5 = you write what each thread does and how it is launched.</li><li><strong>Single-thread abstraction</strong>: 5 = you write one sample and nothing else.</li></ul><p class="axis-note radar-note"><a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, in the full tables</a>.</p></details>
